## 分诊 · `domain:services` / `priority:p2` / `pm:queue`

**Anchor read, not guessed.** `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/**` ⇒ `domain:services`. ⭐ **The DROP-shape site is confirmed verbatim** on `origin/main` `f1d7872` (2026-09-05T00:28:44Z):

```
packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:1292
  const fetched = Array.isArray(rows) ? rows : rows?.records ?? [];
```

⇒ Exactly the union-normalizer shape, at exactly the cited line.

### Grade — p2

Same grade and same reasoning as its sibling **#15597** (plugin-auth, 12 blocks), routed alongside:

- **7 of the 28 `records`-limb source blocks**, in the **security** plugin — dead limbs that *read as a contract* are worst in packages where the next author will copy the defensive shape.
- ⭐ **One of the seven is the opposite defect**: `security-plugin.ts:1292` is also **#15092's DROP shape** — its trailing filter **silently drops a malformed row instead of gapping** — and **must be repaired in the opposite direction from the other six.** ⛔ A uniform sweep would either leave it dropping or "tidy" it into the same shape as its neighbours. This is the sentence to carry into the dispatch.
- Not p1 (dead code is unreachable; the DROP block needs a malformed row). Not p3 (7 sites, in security, one actively wrong).

### Boundary test — Bug/tidy, no manual floor

Removing an unreachable limb and replacing a silent filter with a gap/refusal both restore declared = enforced. ⛔ **No gate change** — #15094 ruled against widening (precision **0.446 / 0.857** measured) — and ⛔ **no `packages/spec` change.**

### ⭐ The #14843 standard, and the clause that gets skipped

> Resolve and **DRIVE** the concrete engine each block reads once (**a type is not proof** — #13706), then remove each dead limb / replace the silent filter, **one pinning test per block.**

⛔ **Do not delete 7 limbs on the strength of `IDataEngine.find`'s declared `Promise<any[]>`.** #13706 is this repo's own counter-example — a `find()` that never resolves to an array — and it is cited precisely so the shortcut is not taken. **7 blocks, 7 drives, 7 pins.**

### Sizing, and the ordering inside it

Smaller than #15597 (7 vs 13 sites) and in one file for at least the named site, so this is the cheaper of the pair and a reasonable first slice of the family. ⭐ **Do `security-plugin.ts:1292` first and alone** — it is the only one where today's behaviour is *wrong* rather than merely dead, and batching it is how its opposite direction gets lost.

⛔ **Stays a separate card from #15597**: different package, different owner-read, different concrete engine to resolve. Neither blocks the other, and ⛔ they should not be merged into one "dead limb sweep" — the whole point of the #14843 standard is that each block is measured, not swept.

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only.

## Landed — `06c762e25`

PR [#15838](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/15838) is on `main`: `fix(plugin-security): retire seven dead \`{ records }\` find-result limbs, and stop the permission-set loader inventing an empty page (#15838)`. Landing authority `git log origin/main | grep -c '(#15838)'` = 1, cwd control `(#15365)` = 1. `pm:dispatched` stripped; the card keeps `bug`, `priority:p2`, `domain:services`, `finding`, read back to confirm.

### Six limbs removed — and the seventh repaired in the opposite direction

The census re-derived as **7 blocks / 9 grep lines / 6 files**, zero delta from the card, anchored on the **limb** `.records` rather than on the ternary — which is what catches `normalize-managed-by.ts:55`'s guard-clause spelling that a ternary-anchored scan misses. All seven were **driven** on a real `ObjectQL` over a real `SqlDriver`, with attribution taken from the source line that issued the call rather than from the block's own label. Every seam answered a bare array on a populated page and an empty one alike.

⭐ **The seventh was the opposite defect.** `security-plugin.ts`'s `sys_permission_set` loader mapped **three different facts onto one value**: an empty catalog, a read that **threw** (`catch { rows = [] }`), and a result it could not read (`?? []`). Only the first is an answer. That mattered because the consumer had **already declared the handling**: `PermissionEvaluator.resolvePermissionSets` catches a throwing loader, stays fail-closed and names the failure in a warn — precisely so that *"a transient DB error"* does not make permission sets *"silently vanish"* with *"undiagnosable"* 403s (#2565). ⇒ **The loader swallowing its own read failure made that warn unreachable.** The diagnostic this repo had already built could never fire; a DB outage and an empty catalog produced identical 403s.

It now propagates, and an unreadable page refuses with `PermissionSetReadUnansweredError` (`DATABASE_ERROR`, ADR-0112's existing vocabulary — no `packages/spec` change).

### The enforcement claim was measured in both directions, and the first version of it was wrong

The PR originally said enforcement was *"unchanged in both directions"*. The review drove `resolvePermissionSets` through this PR's own `dbLoaderFor(ORG)` at HEAD **and at the merge-base blob**, on five engine conditions:

| input | base → HEAD |
|---|---|
| healthy page | identical |
| read throws | `[]` → `[]`, warn **0 → 1** |
| `undefined` resolve | identical |
| **envelope** | granted → **`[]`** |
| **page with a non-object element** | granted → **`[]`** |

⇒ Identical on **every result the shipped engine produces**, with the throw never escaping the request path; it refuses only on two shapes that engine cannot produce. Both fail-closed, both a **declared** narrowing. ⚠️ The unqualified sentence was corrected before landing, and this was the third of five instances this session where the one clause that turned out false was **the clause no pin covered**.

### Two gates went red first and were repaired — which is the control

`check:engine-double-contract` (the pin's forwarding recorder is an engine double; the ledger gained two rows, so the ratchet **grew**) and `check:system-context-census` (pure line rot — every anchor off by exactly the +66 this change adds, repaired with the gate's own `--fix`, line numbers only). ⭐ A gate family reporting 93/93 green means nothing unless something in it can go red; these two are that proof.

### The merge, which was not routine

⚠️ This PR sat with GitHub reporting `mergeable_state: dirty` while `git merge-tree --write-tree` exited **0 with no conflict markers** — because `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` carries `merge=os-regen` and **GitHub's server-side merge does not run local merge drivers** (#15885's corollary, met in the wild). ⭐ And the resolution was not pure line rot: `--fix` **refused** with *"the page anchors 9 distinct line(s) … but the tree holds 8 anchorable line(s). The POPULATION changed, this is not a shift"*, because upstream `f9a3c3216` had added a row citing the **same** site as row 1. Pointing the two at one site was a structural decision made by hand; the generator produced every number. ⛔ No anchor was hand-written.

`security-plugin.ts`'s blob necessarily differs from the reviewed head because that same upstream commit touched it. The authored delta was proven unchanged by hashing the **content lines** of the diff (headers dropped so `@@` offsets cannot move it): `258a6439350d…` on both sides, with an unrelated file through the same measure returning a different hash as the control.

### Left open deliberately

**#15840** — three seams still report an un-happened read as `[]`. ⚠️ Regraded **p1** this session on the review's measurement: `reconcileOrgAdminGrant`'s `sys_member` read enters the **revoke** branch on a fault and **deletes a standing grant** — a persisting withdrawal, not a passive gap. The card's restraint was right for the other two; the shared reasoning did not distinguish *reports* from *writes*.
